findings.title: Error re-selection compares the untrimmed posted value while validator and writer trim — crafted whitespace choice renders with neither radio checked
findings.evidence: references.gleam:237 `selected: common.get_val(values, reference_attestation.field_name),` vs reference_attestation.gleam:50 `case common.get_val(values, field_name) |> string.trim {` and application_handler.gleam:2253 `Ok(value) -> string.trim(value)`; view_option: `let checked_attrs = case value == selected {`
findings.detail: validate_choice trims, get_form_value (insert/ack/confirmation paths) trims, but the error re-render reader does not. A crafted POST of ' attested ' validates and persists, yet re-renders unchecked if another field errors. Crafted-POST only; browser `required` makes it self-correcting on resubmit. Contradicts the module's own 'validator and writer must agree' invariant.
findings.recommended_fix: Pass `common.get_val(values, reference_attestation.field_name) |> string.trim` as `selected` in references.gleam.

findings.title: Yes-path §5.4 confirmation line: finalise_application flag wiring has no test (PARTIAL, P1)
findings.evidence: `reference_contact_attested: get_form_value(values, reference_attestation.field_name) == reference_attestation.attested_value,` — integration tests gdpr_integration_test.gleam:2487/2568 assert resp.status and DB rows only, never the response body
findings.detail: view_confirmation_page is unit-tested both flag ways, but the derivation hop is untested: flipping the comparison to declined_value passes every test in the suite.
findings.recommended_fix: Assert simulate.read_body(resp) contains ref-attestation-confirmation in the attested integration test, and its absence in the declined one.

findings.title: Attestation error span combines role="alert" with aria-live="polite", contradicting the documented house rule
findings.evidence: reference_attestation.gleam: `attribute("role", "alert"),` + `attribute("aria-live", "polite"),` vs form_pages.gleam:377-379 comment: `role="alert" implies aria-live="assertive"; setting aria-live="polite" alongside creates inconsistent announcements across screen readers.`
findings.detail: The house pattern deliberately keeps role="alert" alone and lets the implicit assertive live region work; the new span reintroduces the combination the comment says to avoid.
findings.recommended_fix: Drop the explicit aria-live attribute, keep role="alert" alone.

findings.title: 'Your landlord will ring them' helper survives in the landlord group — same contradiction the §5.2 intro replacement removed
findings.evidence: references.gleam:28 `"Your landlord will ring them \u{2014} so name, phone, and email, please."`
findings.detail: Only true on the declined path. Deliberately deferred per the spec's Ask-First and flagged as open question #2 in the PR body with a ruling requested — process followed; the contradiction itself is real and unresolved.
findings.recommended_fix: Resolve the open question: reword the helper to match the attestation model in a follow-up.

findings.title: Spec leaves the sprint-status task unchecked while the same diff performs the flip and the spec declares status: done
findings.evidence: `- [ ] `sprint-status-refcheck-v1.yaml` -- status flips -- bookkeeping per briefing (done at badge-out)` vs diff: `-  rc1-2-attestation-ui-the-references-section-choice: backlog` / `+  rc1-2-attestation-ui-the-references-section-choice: done`
findings.detail: Spec task list contradicts the PR's own contents; task text says the tick happens at badge-out, so this self-resolves — cosmetic bookkeeping drift inside the PR.
findings.recommended_fix: Tick the task when the status flip ships (badge-out), as the task text itself says.

findings.title: review_loop_iteration: 0 contradicts the documented review-round-1 amendment
findings.evidence: front matter `review_loop_iteration: 0` vs Spec Change Log `**Trigger (review round 1):** blind-hunter — every bug-hunt scenario that submits `/apply` fails post-merge…`
findings.detail: Metadata counter disagrees with the change log that records a completed review round 1 amendment.

findings.title: Spec Code Map omits form_view_test.gleam, which the diff modifies
findings.evidence: Code Map lists only reference_attestation_test.gleam and form_pages_test.gleam; diff contains `diff --git a/server/test/application/form_view_test.gleam`
findings.detail: Three test files change; the Code Map documents two. Minor doc omission.

findings.title: Attested-derivation expression duplicated verbatim at two handler sites instead of one helper
findings.evidence: Site 1 (~1539): `get_form_value(values, reference_attestation.field_name) == reference_attestation.attested_value,` — Site 2 (~2150): `reference_contact_attested: get_form_value(values, reference_attestation.field_name,) == reference_attestation.attested_value,`
findings.detail: Same two-constant comparison spelled out twice. A public is_attested(values) on reference_attestation keeps one owner and is the natural companion to validate_choice the stepper lifts on rebase.
findings.recommended_fix: Add `pub fn is_attested(values) -> Bool` to reference_attestation; call it at both sites.

findings.title: Error-state aria-describedby join (help + error id) has no assertion
findings.evidence: `attribute("aria-describedby", case has_err { True -> "ref-attestation-help " <> error_id ...` — card_error_state_shows_message_and_has_error_test asserts only has-error, the message, and role="alert"
findings.detail: The error-branch describedby join (added per the spec's own review amendment) is unpinned; dropping it passes all tests.
findings.recommended_fix: Assert aria-describedby="ref-attestation-help field-reference_contact_choice-error" and the error span id in the error-state test.

findings.title: Vacuous "required" assertion — satisfied by aria-required even if the radio required attribute is dropped
findings.evidence: `html |> string.contains("required") |> should.be_true` while the card already renders `attribute("aria-required", "true")`
findings.detail: aria-required contains the substring 'required', so the AC's 'radio pair is required' HTML attribute is effectively unpinned.
findings.recommended_fix: Assert the rendered bare-attribute form (e.g. "required type=\"radio\"", attributes render name-sorted) or exactly two bare required occurrences.

findings.title: Advisory test gate: PASS
findings.detail: P0 100%: choice-required, tamper rejection, attested/declined persistence, and the unsubmittable-form trap all pinned at unit + integration (validate_choice unit tests, gdpr_integration write-path tests incl. missing-choice, full-form render test, updated bug-hunt E2E fixtures). P1 ~93%: the Yes-confirmation chain is PARTIAL at the handler-wiring hop. Overall ~97%, level mix appropriate. Gate claims spot-checked and confirmed in verification.
findings.recommended_fix: The two response-body assertions from the warning finding lift P1 to ~100%.

rejected_findings.title: seed-applicants.yaml documents reference_contact_choice as submitted but adds no executable step
rejected_findings.reason: False positive: the scenario is a runtime-materialization protocol — the description block IS the instruction the executing agent authors the payload from, and the submit JS iterates formData dynamically (`for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(app.formData)) fd.set(k, String(v))`, line 400). There is no static payload to update; the description update is the correct and only change.

rejected_findings.title: Re-selection tests assert checked before data-testid though the attribute list appends checked after
rejected_findings.reason: False positive: Lustre SSR renders attributes name-sorted (checked < data-testid); the test file itself documents this ('Lustre renders the empty attribute as a bare checked immediately before data-testid'), and CI unit tests pass green at the reviewed sha.
